faqs.q: What is a 304 Stainless Steel Lap Joint Flange used for?
faqs.a: The 304 Stainless Steel Lap Joint Flange is a lap joint flange in forged 304 stainless steel: a loose flange that rides on a stub end, so the bolt holes line up by turning the flange; only the stub end touches the fluid. This listing holds 4 part numbers, 3/4" to 12" NPS, in Class 300.

faqs.q: How do I read part number IH-PF-LJ-D4-040 on the 304 Lap Joint Flange?
faqs.a: IH-PF-LJ-D4-040 is a 304 lap joint flange in 10" NPS: the block D4 carries the class and grade, and the last block 040 is the size. In this listing D4 is Class 300. Size codes are the nominal size in sixteenths of an inch.

faqs.q: What sizes and classes does the 304 Lap Joint Flange come in?
faqs.a: The 304 Stainless Steel Lap Joint Flange is listed in 4 part numbers from 3/4" to 12" NPS, in Class 300. For example, IH-PF-LJ-D4-12 is 3/4" NPS Class 300 lap joint; IH-PF-LJ-D4-040 is 10" NPS Class 300 lap joint; IH-PF-LJ-D4-192 is 12" NPS Class 300 lap joint. Sizes outside the table are quoted on request.

faqs.q: How do I choose the right class and size of 304 Lap Joint Flange?
faqs.a: Choose the 304 Stainless Steel Lap Joint Flange by NPS size and class, then pair it with a stub end of the same size and grade. This listing is Class 300, in 3/4" to 12" NPS, so the flange class and the stub end schedule are set separately.

faqs.q: What pressure is the 304 Lap Joint Flange rated for?
faqs.a: The 304 Stainless Steel Lap Joint Flange is rated by the pressure and temperature tables of ASME B16.5 for Material Group 2.1 (304 stainless steel), and the allowable pressure falls as temperature rises. This listing is Class 300. Tell us the design pressure and temperature and we will confirm the class.

faqs.q: Should I choose 304 or 316 for the 304 Lap Joint Flange?
faqs.a: The 304 Stainless Steel Lap Joint Flange is made from 304 stainless steel. 304 suits fresh water, food and general process service; 316 adds molybdenum for better resistance to chlorides and pitting. The same type is listed in 316 as the [316 version](/p/316-stainless-steel-lap-joint-flange).

faqs.q: Which standard does the 304 Lap Joint Flange follow, and can I get certificates?
faqs.a: The 304 Stainless Steel Lap Joint Flange is made to ASME B16.5, which sets the dimensions, classes and pressure and temperature ratings of pipe flanges. This listing holds no test certificate or declaration; if your job needs a material certificate, ask for it in the enquiry so it can be requested before supply.

faqs.q: What does the 304 Lap Joint Flange connect to, and are gaskets and bolts included?
faqs.a: The 304 Stainless Steel Lap Joint Flange is a loose flange that rides on a stub end, so it needs a stub end of the same size, and only the stub end touches the fluid. Use the [304 Stainless Steel MSS SP-43 Type A Stub End](/p/304-stainless-steel-mss-sp-43-type-a-stub-end) or a Type C stub end. Gaskets and stud bolts are ordered separately, to suit the class and service.

faqs.q: How is the 304 Lap Joint Flange fitted to the pipe?
faqs.a: The 304 Stainless Steel Lap Joint Flange is slid over the stub end, then turned to line up the bolt holes. Use a welding procedure suited to stainless steel, and tighten the stud bolts evenly in a cross pattern. See our [guide to stainless flanges to ASME B16.5](/blog/stainless-steel-flanges-asme-b16-5).

faqs.q: What is the difference between the 304 Lap Joint Flange and the 304 MSS SP-43 Type A Stub End?

The first is a loose flange that rides on a stub end, so the bolt holes line up by turning the flange; the second is a forged lap with a radiused back that matches a lap joint flange, butt-welded to the pipe.
